summary.title: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference
summary.one_liner: A quantization scheme and co-designed training procedure that let neural networks run inference with integer-only arithmetic on CPUs while keeping accuracy, shown on MobileNets for ImageNet classification and COCO detection.
keywords: efficient deep learning on mobile devices
how to run neural networks with integer math
takeaways: Inference can be run entirely with integer-only arithmetic, which can be faster than floating-point inference on common integer hardware.
A training procedure is co-designed with the quantization scheme to preserve end-to-end accuracy after quantization.
The approach improves the accuracy versus on-device latency tradeoff, including for already efficient MobileNets.
Results are demonstrated on ImageNet classification and COCO detection on popular CPUs.
summary.summary: This arXiv paper (submitted December 2017, cs.LG) proposes a quantization scheme that performs neural network inference using integer-only arithmetic, along with a training procedure designed to keep model accuracy after quantization. According to the abstract, the scheme improves the accuracy and on-device latency tradeoff, with significant gains even on MobileNets. The authors demonstrate the method on ImageNet classification and COCO detection on popular CPUs. The listing describes it as defining the affine scale and zero-point scheme with integer accumulation, but the page text itself shows only the abstract and metadata, so the detailed method is not visible here.
